questions: Which inputs feed the AND gate, and which feeds the NOT gate?
Which gate output actually drives the alarm?
segments.say: Meet the circuit. Inputs A and B feed the AND gate, input C feeds the NOT gate, and both gate outputs meet at the OR gate, whose output drives the alarm. Point at each gate on your student notes diagram before any signal travels.

questions: What is the AND output when A and B are both 1?
What is the first truth table row, including NOT C?
segments.say: A and B on: the AND path lights the alarm. With both at 1 the AND output is 1, the signal travels through the OR gate to the alarm, and the first truth table row fills in. Now try the gate questions on your worksheet.

questions: Why does B at 0 force the AND output to 0?
What two values reach the OR gate in this scene?
segments.say: B off and C on: the alarm stays off. B at 0 forces the AND output to 0, and C at 1 makes NOT C 0 as well, so the OR gate receives nothing. Check this row against your student notes before moving on.

questions: How can the alarm be on when the AND output is 0?
Which truth table rows have the alarm on, and what decides them?
segments.say: C off: NOT C alone lights the alarm. The NOT gate flips C from 0 to 1, that signal travels through the OR gate, and the alarm switches on even though the AND output is 0. Keep the gate-by-gate order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
segments.watchFor: The alarm is on whenever A is on, because OR works just like AND. Listen for students who jump straight from input A to the alarm. Send them back to scene 3 and scene 4: Read the circuit gate by gate: the alarm is on only when (A AND B) are both 1 or NOT C is 1 - that is, when A and B are both on, or C is off (or both).
